title: Information, Referral, and Relocation
intro: We connect service members and their families to valuable resources, helping them successfully navigate their military journey.

sections.heading: Welcome Aboard
sections.markdown:
Helping you navigate relocation and connect to your community.

#### Welcome Aboard Brief

Discover essential information and resources to help you and your family adjust smoothly to life at your new duty station.

**Topics discussed will include:**

• Base Services and Amenities - Overview of essential services, such as medical facilities, commissary, exchange, and fitness centers.
• Relocation Assistance - Guidance on housing, transportation, and accessing resources through the Relocation Assistance Program (RAP).
• Childcare and School Information - Details on childcare options, school enrollment, and youth programs to support your family.
• Sponsorship and Family Readiness - Introduction to the Sponsorship Program and Family Readiness Officers (FRO) for ongoing support and connection to your new community.
• Local Area Orientation - Information on local attractions, shopping, dining, and community activities to help you settle in and explore your new surroundings.

View the event calendar for scheduled Welcome Aboard Briefs or reach out to the Information, Referral, and Relocation office for availability and registration.

sections.heading: Permanent Change of Station (PCS)
sections.markdown: Providing resources and support for your PCS journey.

sections.heading: PCS Workshop
sections.markdown:
The Permanent Change of Station (PCS) Workshop is designed to guide Marines and their families through every step of the relocation process. Whether it's your first move or one of many, our workshop provides valuable insights and resources to help you transition with ease.

**Nine reasons to attend a PCS Workshop:**

1. It's Mandatory - Per MCO 1754.10B, attending the PCS Workshop is required for a smooth transition to your new duty station.
2. Installation-Specific Information and Contacts - Get valuable information about your new installation, including key contacts and local services.
3. Household Goods Weight Allowances & Entitlements - Learn about your weight allowances for household goods and what entitlements you can access during your move.
4. Travel Allowances, Budget, and Government Card - Understand your travel allowances, how to budget for the move, and how to use your government travel card.
5. Moving with Pets - Receive guidance on transporting pets, quarantine regulations, and other related requirements.
6. School Liaison & Exceptional Family Member Program Resources - Access support for school enrollment and resources for family members with special needs.
7. Spouse Employment Opportunities - Discover job search assistance and career development resources for spouses.
8. Personalized Relocation Plan & Online Relocation Resources - Create a customized relocation plan and explore online resources to streamline your move.
9. Request a Sponsor - As per MCO 1320.11H, learn how to request a sponsor to help you adjust and settle into your new duty station.

Don't move alone. Contact your Information, Referral, and Relocation specialist to schedule your appointment today.

sections.heading: Relocation Assistance
sections.markdown:
Relocation Assistance is designed to help make your move as smooth as possible, offering a variety of services to support Marines and their families during the transition to a new duty station.

Relocation support includes:

• Housing - Get help finding on-base or off-base housing, temporary lodging, and understanding your options.
• Local Area Information - Access guides and insights on the local community, including schools, healthcare, and recreational activities.
• PCS Workshops - Attend workshops covering the entire relocation process. Receive guidance on budgeting for your move, managing expenses, and planning for financial stability during the relocation process.
• Request a Sponsor - Connecting with a sponsor at your new installation is an important step for a successful transition.
• Lending Locker Access - Borrow essential household items like kitchenware and small appliances while waiting for your household goods to arrive.

sections.heading: Request a Sponsor
sections.markdown:
Connecting with your sponsor prior to your PCS move is an important step for a successful transition. Your sponsor is here to guide you through the challenges of relocation and help you integrate into your new community.

Sponsors support includes:

• Personalized Guidance - Receive tailored advice on housing, transportation, and base services.
• Quick Access to Resources - Get connected to key resources such as medical facilities, childcare, and recreation centers.
• Streamlined PCS Process - Navigate administrative tasks, like check-ins and paperwork, more efficiently.
• Support Network - Build connections within the base and local community, reducing the stress of transitioning to a new environment.

Request a sponsor by submitting the Sponsorship Request Form to the Information, Referral, and Relocation office.

sections.heading: Explore Housing Options
sections.markdown: Connecting you with housing and your military community.

sections.heading: Base Housing
sections.markdown:
Base housing offers Marines and their families a comfortable and supportive living environment, making the transition to a new duty station smoother and more manageable. Living on base fosters a sense of community and connection, allowing families to quickly integrate into their new surroundings and access essential services.

**Important steps to securing base housing:**

1. Apply Early - Start the housing application process as soon as you receive your Permanent Change of Station (PCS) orders to secure your spot on the waiting list. Contact the housing office within 72 hours of arriving at your new installation.
2. Gather Required Documents - Prepare necessary documentation, including your PCS orders, ID, and any other relevant paperwork required by the housing office.
3. Contact the Housing Offices - Reach out to the base housing office for information on available units, policies, and specific requirements.
4. Schedule a Housing Inspection - Once assigned a unit, arrange for an inspection to ensure it meets your family's needs and is ready for occupancy.
5. Plan Your Move - Coordinate your moving logistics, including transportation of your household goods and any temporary lodging if needed.

Taking these steps will help ensure a smooth transition into base housing, allowing you and your family to settle in quickly and enjoy your new community.

Contact the Information, Referral, and Relocation for more information about housing at your new location.

sections.heading: Support for Service Members and Families
sections.markdown: Exploring resources and tools to help you and your family thrive.

sections.heading: Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS)
sections.markdown:
Connecting to the [Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System](https://milconnect.dmdc.osd.mil/milconnect/) (DEERS) office is important for Marines and their families to ensure they receive the military benefits and services. The DEERS office provides support for enrollment and updates, helping to maintain accurate records for eligibility.

Support includes:

• Enrollment and Updates - Assistance with enrolling in DEERS and updating personal information such as address, marital status, and dependent information.
• ID Card Issuance - Issuance and renewal of military ID cards for service members and their eligible family members.
• Benefits Verification - Confirmation of eligibility for healthcare, education, and other military benefits.
• TRICARE Enrollment - Guidance on enrolling in TRICARE for healthcare coverage and accessing medical services.

Connecting with the DEERS office ensures that you and your family can effectively access and manage your military benefits.

sections.heading: Child Care
sections.markdown:
Child Care services are essential for Marines and their families new to an installation, providing a safe and nurturing environment for children while offering crucial support to parents during their transition.

The following services are designed to support your family's needs, helping your children thrive in their new environment.

Child Care services available include:

• Child Development Centers (CDC) - Full-day care for infants and preschool-aged children, promoting early learning and development. Some CDCs offer hourly child care. Check with your local CDC for availability.
• Family Child Care (FCC) - Home-based care options that offer personalized attention in a family-like setting.
• Before and After School Programs - Supervised care for school-aged children, ensuring they have a safe place during non-school hours.
• New Parent Support Program (NPSP) - Resources and guidance for new parents, including home visits, parenting classes, and workshops.

Visit [militarychildcare.com](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome) to enroll your child into one of the Child Development Centers.

When registering make sure you have your children(s) updated immunization records available.

sections.heading: School Liaison
sections.markdown:
The School Liaison is a vital resource for Marines and their families new to an installation, helping to ensure a seamless transition for children into local schools. By providing essential information and support, the School Liaison assists families in navigating educational options and addressing any concerns related to their child's education.

School Liaison support include:

• School Enrollment - Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.
• Local School Information - Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.
• Home School Information - Assisting families with guidance on registering with the DoDEA schools.
• Exceptional Family Member Support - Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services.
• Transition Assistance - Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

These services help ensure that children receive the support they need for a successful educational experience in their new community.

For more information about support and services, visit the School Liaison webpage on the MCCS website.

sections.heading: Exceptional Family Member Program
sections.markdown:
The Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) is essential for service members and their families with special needs, providing support and resources to ensure a smooth transition to a new installation.

EFMP helps families navigate the challenges associated with relocating by connecting them to specialized services and community resources tailored to their unique circumstances.

EFMP Services Available Include:

• Enrollment Assistance - Guidance on enrolling in the EFMP and understanding program requirements.
• Specialized Support Services - Access to resources for medical, educational, and emotional support tailored to family members with special needs.
• Transition Assistance - Help with relocating to a new area, including information on local schools, medical facilities, and community services.
• Advocacy and Resources - Connection to advocacy services and local support groups to assist families in accessing necessary care and benefits.
• Workshops and Training - Opportunities for families to participate in workshops focused on managing special needs and navigating available resources.

Learn more about how EFMP supports you and your family by visiting [EFMP](https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program).

sections.heading: Lending Locker
sections.markdown:
The Lending Locker is an invaluable resource for Marines and their families, offering essential household items to borrow temporarily while awaiting the arrival of personal belongings during a relocation. This service helps ease the transition by providing the necessary tools needed without the immediate expense of purchasing items.

Available Items _May_ Include:

• Kitchenware (pots, pans, dishes, utensils)
• Small appliances (microwaves, toasters, coffee makers)

Take advantage of the Lending Locker to help make your move as seamless as possible!

_Not all items are available at all locations._

Contact the Information, Referral, and Relocation office to learn more about the Lending Locker.

sections.heading: Family Member Travel Screening Cell
sections.markdown:
One of the most challenging parts of moving overseas is the suitability screening process – it can be confusing and complex. The Family Member Travel Screening Cell helps Marines and families successfully navigate the screening process by providing proactive support throughout the process.

Support includes:

• Providing detailed information on the screening process.
• Connecting Marines and families with the appropriate medical screening office.
• Ensuring the timely initiation and completion of screening.
• Resolving issues with medical screening offices.
• Offering transparency of screening status for Marines, families, monitors, and commands.
• Training and assisting commands in their screening-related roles.

For assistance, send an email to SMB_HQMC_FMTS@usmc.mil.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
sections.markdown:
**What services does the Information, Referral, and Relocation program provide?**
The program helps connect Marines and their families to valuable resources that include housing, relocation, childcare, schools, and access to community resources.

**How can I request a sponsor for my move?**
You can request a sponsor by contacting the program directly or through your unit's command, and we will match you with a Sponsor.

**What should I do if I need temporary lodging during my move?**
You can access temporary lodging options through our program, which can provide a comfortable place to stay while you secure permanent housing.

**Are there resources available for spouses seeking employment at my new duty station?**
Yes, the [Family Member Employment Assistance](https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/family-member-employment-assistance-program) offers employment resources for spouses, including job search assistance, resume writing support, and networking opportunities.

**How do I update my DEERS information after relocating?**
You can update your DEERS information by visiting the ID Card Center or using the online [ID Card Office Online](https://idco.dmdc.osd.mil/idco/) portal to ensure your benefits remain active.
